## The decision this serves

A notebook that ran in two minutes on the demo has now been running six hours on a full section. Decide what you needed to know before you started.

::: {.callout-important}
**Scale.** Runs in 25 min, peak memory chunked a few GB versus eager tens of GB.
Watch **chunk size, relative to your access pattern** — that is what stops being safe on a full section.
:::

## Concept

Zarr and Parquet backing, chunking, and lazy access; where the object model lets you avoid loading everything at once.

**The assumption that breaks first.** That an operation which was cheap on the toy tier stays cheap at section scale.

## Failure mode

**What it produces.** A notebook that works on the toy tier is run on a full section and silently swaps for hours instead of failing fast.

**The diagnostic that catches it.** Profile peak memory on a subsample and extrapolate before running the whole thing.
